decisions.rationale: It reports only general improvement on most metrics and two examples, omitting the five-metric pattern and the XNLI and Lambada decreases.
It claims higher MMLU than simple methods in both settings, but in 1B Method M tied ZeroEmbed and was slightly below MeanEmbed.
The passage notes no statistical tests but omits the single-evaluation design and all specified missing-standard-error limitations.
It incorrectly describes Method M as having higher WikiText scores, although its advantage is lower bits per byte, and omits three accuracy benchmarks.
It reports only general improvement on most metrics and two examples, without identifying the five improvements or two tiny decreases.
It claims Method M was higher on MMLU, ARC-C, and GSM8K, but the 1B results contain ties and a slight MMLU deficit.
Only the absence of statistical tests is reported; the single evaluation and unavailable standard errors are omitted.
“Matched or slightly exceeded” understates the four substantial advantages and omits that FOCUS outperformed Method M on GSM8K.
The passage gives general similarity plus MMLU and WikiText examples, but omits the ARC-C, GSM8K, and Belebele relationships.
It reports a gap on ARC-C despite exact preservation and omits Method M’s worse Belebele performance.
It notes absent statistical tests but does not report the single evaluation or the metrics lacking standard errors.
The passage correctly covers MMLU, ARC-C, GSM8K, and WikiText relative to the original model but omits the Belebele decline.
The broad better-preservation claim and selected examples do not report superiority across all six accuracy benchmarks and lower WikiText in the 12B setting.
It summarizes improvement on most metrics but omits the complete five-improvement and two-decrease pattern.
General near-equivalence within 0.01 does not report the exact ties, slight MMLU deficit to MeanEmbed, or Belebele and WikiText advantages.
The passage reports no statistical tests but omits the single-evaluation design and the specified missing standard errors.
